claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Laser surface alloying with a pre-placed 2–5 µm Al powder layer will create an Al-enriched surface zone.
High scanning speeds and controlled beam power will produce rapid surface melting and solidification.
The laser treatment can locally incorporate Al without introducing damaging defects.
Laser alloying will distribute Al uniformly through the near-surface region.
The Al-enriched surface zone will form a continuous alumina scale during exposure to air at 800 °C.
The alumina scale formed on the treated alloy will be adherent.
Al in the enriched surface region will selectively oxidize to form protective alpha-Al2O3.
The alumina barrier will inhibit further oxygen ingress.
The surface-localized treatment will leave the bulk microstructure intact.
Laser Al alloying will reduce oxide-scale growth relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The treatment will improve oxygen resistance in air at 800 °C for exposure durations up to 100 hours.
The treatment will maintain or only minimally reduce room-temperature tensile ductility relative to untreated material.
The treatment will maintain or only minimally reduce yield strength at temperatures up to 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation and has insufficient high-temperature oxygen resistance.
